questions.title: If the Boston Celtics agree to trade Jaylen Brown by July 31, 2026, which NBA team will be his destination?
questions.background: Jaylen Brown plays for the Boston Celtics and was named the 2024 NBA Finals MVP.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Reporting by ESPN or The Associated Press identifying an agreed trade involving Jaylen Brown between June 1 and July 31, 2026. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the team designated to receive Brown under the first such publicly reported agreement. An agreement counts even if league approval or completion remains pending. Accepted Answer Format : The full name of the NBA team.
questions.current_reasoning: On June 24-25, ESPN's Shams Charania reported Boston remains 'actively engaged' in Jaylen Brown trade talks with a 'sense of purpose,' Sports Illustrated's Chris Mannix reported the Celtics are 'hunting a big man' and willing to deal Brown for one, and ClutchPoints (June 25) confirmed that both the Houston Rockets and New Orleans Pelicans have held active trade dialogue with Boston (noting long-standing Celtics interest in Trey Murphy III), while Minnesota dropped out after acquiring LaMelo Ball. Meanwhile, Atlanta (#8) and the Clippers (#5) both kept their 2026 lottery picks during the draft, trimming their near-term leverage, and Portland was absent from June 25 beat reporting. Conditional on a trade occurring by July 31, Houston strengthens as the consensus favorite (25%) and New Orleans rises sharply to #2 (16%), ahead of Atlanta (14%), the Clippers (9%), and Portland (7%), with 29% left on the rest of the NBA.

questions.title: Which month will the Palestinian Football Association announce for the resumption of its football competitions after their October 2023 suspension?
questions.background: Palestinian football competitions have been suspended since the war in Gaza began in October 2023.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official Palestinian Football Association announcement, or reliable news reporting quoting its leadership. Resolution Conditions : Use the first public announcement between July 1 and August 31, 2026, that specifies a date for restarting the suspended football competitions. Resolve to the calendar month containing that announced restart date, regardless of whether competitions subsequently begin as scheduled. If no qualifying announcement occurs by the deadline, the question is void. Accepted Answer Format : The full English name of the month, not the month in which the announcement is made.
questions.current_reasoning: Gaza hosted a PFA-supervised 5-a-side recovery tournament in Feb–Mar 2026 following the Oct 2025 ceasefire, while Al Jazeera reported on June 14, 2026 that the West Bank / Palestine Professional League remains suspended with hopes of a scaled-down revival 'after the summer break concludes.' Historically the Palestinian domestic season begins in late August or September, and an announcement made between July 1 and August 31 would typically allow 4–8 weeks of lead time for squad registration and logistics. Conditioning on a qualifying announcement, September (0.33), August (0.23), and October (0.22) capture the core window, with November (0.09), July (0.06), and a 7% tail for December or later.

questions.title: Which Russian official will the Kremlin publicly confirm as attending Ali Khamenei's state funeral?
questions.background: Iran's supreme leader Ali Khamenei was killed on February 28, 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the Russian official whose planned attendance at Ali Khamenei's state funeral is publicly confirmed by the Kremlin. Use the Kremlin's announcement or reliable reporting of it. This question concerns the announcement, not actual attendance. Resolution Date : 2026-07-02 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the official's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Iran rescheduled Ali Khamenei's state funeral to July 4-9, 2026, and President Pezeshkian only began issuing foreign invitations around June 23-24. Strong precedent favors State Duma Speaker Vyacheslav Volodin, whom the Kremlin sent to lead Russia's delegations to both Ebrahim Raisi's funeral (May 2024) and Pezeshkian's inauguration (July 2024), while Vladimir Putin is very unlikely to travel to Tehran shortly after a four-month air war. Because Khamenei was Supreme Leader and heads of government like Pakistan's PM are expected, Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin, Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, Federation Council Chairwoman Valentina Matviyenko, and Security Council Secretary Sergei Shoigu are the main alternatives, leaving 16% tail mass on Putin, Dmitry Medvedev, Alexander Novak, or other envoys.

local_articles.title: Kremlin Aware of Viral Video Threatening Armed Uprising Over Alleged Abuses in Army
local_articles.snippet: The Kremlin said Friday it was aware of, but had not yet seen, a viral video featuring a Russian man identifying himself as a Ukraine war veteran who threatened to stage an armed uprising unless President Vladimir Putin met with him to discuss the alleged abuse of soldiers by military commanders. local_articles.title: Kremlin says it will look into ‘strange’ video alleging army torture
local_articles.snippet: MOSCOW – The Kremlin said on June 26 it would look into a viral video appeal to President Vladimir Putin by a military veteran accusing Russian commanders in Ukraine of torturing and murdering soldiers for not fulfilling “suicidal orders”. Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the Kremlin had not yet seen the appeal, which was posted on Instagram, but that it sounded like it contained “strange wording”. The post by veteran Alexander Lunin, which did not cite any evidence or name any alleged victims or perpetrators, garnered over 12 million views in 24 hours. Instagram is banned in Russia and can be accessed only by using a virtual private network. Before his video appeal, most Russians had not heard of Lunin, who lives in Russia’s Voronezh region. questions.title: Which NBA team will sign Trey Alexander to a two-way contract in the first two weeks of July 2026?
questions.background: A two-way contract allows a player to play for both an NBA team and its G League affiliate.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : as confirmed by a team announcement or contemporaneous sports reporting Resolution Date : Resolve to the NBA team that signs Trey Alexander to a two-way contract between July 1 and July 14, 2026, inclusive Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the team's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Trey Alexander (2024-25 G League Rookie of the Year with Denver) spent 2025-26 on a one-year two-way contract with the New Orleans Pelicans, shooting 51.4% FG and 50.0% 3PT in 9 NBA games while playing mainly for Birmingham, and enters the 2026 offseason as a Pelicans restricted two-way free agent per Spotrac. Incumbent RFA rights give New Orleans by far the highest single-team probability (32%) of re-signing him via qualifying offer or new two-way deal in early July, though coaching turnover and post-draft roster cycling leave a ~68% chance he signs elsewhere as Denver let him walk on July 3, 2025. Without specific external rumors as of June 24, the remaining 29 teams each carry low single-digit odds, with modest edges to hometown Oklahoma City, former club Denver, and rebuilding guard-needy teams like Brooklyn and Washington (53% left on the rest of the league).

questions.title: Which U.S. state will have the highest reported cyclospora case count by July 16, 2026?
questions.background: Cyclospora is a parasite that causes intestinal illness. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) monitors reported infections across U.S. states.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The latest CDC state-level data publicly available on July 16, 2026, reporting the cumulative number of cyclospora infections reported during 2026 Resolution Date : 2026-07-16 Accepted Answer Format : String (name of the U.S. state)
questions.current_reasoning: CDC cyclosporiasis surveillance (2018-2025) consistently shows Texas, New York (which includes NYC), and Florida recording the highest cumulative annual case counts; Texas logged 400-788 cases/yr in 2022-2024 (97% in May-Aug) and ramps up earliest due to Mexican produce supply chains, while New York led 2018-2021 genotyped isolates (651 vs Texas 551) and was top alongside Texas and North Carolina in 2025. As of June 18, 2026, FDA's CORE table shows only two small unresolved early-season Cyclospora clusters (8 and 2 cases), so by July 16 base rates heavily favor Texas, New York, and Florida, with 8% left on other states (e.g., North Carolina, Wisconsin, Minnesota, California) in case a localized outbreak hits elsewhere.

questions.title: Which UK party leader will announce plans in early July 2026 to resign as an MP and contest the resulting by-election?
questions.background: A parliamentary resignation can trigger a by-election, which the departing MP may contest to seek a fresh mandate.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public announcements corroborated by contemporaneous reporting from BBC News, The Guardian, or Al Jazeera. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the UK political party leader who publicly announces, between July 1 and July 9, 2026, plans to resign from the House of Commons and stand in the by-election caused by that resignation. The announcement is sufficient; the by-election need not have taken place. Accepted Answer Format : The party leader's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Rupert Lowe (Restore Britain leader, MP for Great Yarmouth) uniquely fits both historical UK precedents for an MP resigning to contest a by-election: he was elected under Reform UK in 2024 before launching Restore Britain in Feb 2026 (which just finished 3rd in Makerfield with ~7%), and on May 15, 2026 he lost his High Court challenge to halt a parliamentary ICGS watchdog probe, creating strong incentive to seek a fresh mandate or preempt a suspension/recall petition. Very few UK party leaders sit in the Commons; Nigel Farage (Reform UK), Jeremy Corbyn (Your Party, elected Independent), Zarah Sultana (ex-Labour/Your Party), and Kemi Badenoch represent smaller tails, with ~12% left for other minor-party MP leaders (e.g., Northern Ireland party leaders or a newly formed breakaway party).

questions.title: Who will Moldova’s parliament elect as prime minister to succeed Alexandru Munteanu?
questions.background: Alexandru Munteanu has resigned as Moldova’s prime minister, triggering his cabinet’s resignation. Moldova is pursuing European Union membership.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Moldovan parliamentary announcements or reliable news reporting confirming the election of a new prime minister. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the first person elected prime minister by Moldova’s parliament following Alexandru Munteanu’s resignation. A nomination or temporary appointment as acting prime minister does not qualify. Resolution Date : The date parliament elects the successor. Accepted Answer Format : The full name of the person elected.
questions.current_reasoning: Moldova's pro-EU ruling party PAS holds a 55/101 parliamentary majority alongside President Maia Sandu, so the successor to PM Alexandru Munteanu (whose Control Corps resigned over loss of trust on June 24, 2026) will be a PAS-backed pick. Top internal cabinet/party contenders are Deputy PM & Foreign Minister Mihai Popșoi, Deputy PM for European Integration Cristina Gherasimov (aligned with the EU accession priority), PAS leader and Speaker Igor Grosu, Deputy PM Vladimir Bolea, and Deputy PM for Economic Development Eugen Osmochescu. Because Sandu and PAS have a strong base rate of tapping surprise technocrats or presidential advisers (as with Dorin Recean in 2023 and Munteanu in Nov 2025), 42% probability mass is left outside the top five.

questions.title: Which company will hold the record for the largest US IPO by a foreign firm as of July 10, 2026?
questions.background: Alibaba's 2014 US initial public offering raised $25 billion, setting the record for the largest US IPO by a foreign company.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official issuer announcements and contemporaneous reporting by reputable news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the company reported as holding the all-time record for the largest US initial public offering by a foreign company as of July 10, 2026. Compare offerings by proceeds raised, not company valuation. An offering whose pricing and share sales have been announced may qualify before exchange trading begins. Accepted Answer Format : The company's commonly used name.
questions.current_reasoning: Following blowout Micron Technology fiscal Q3 earnings ($25.11 adj. EPS vs. $20.78 est., $41.46B revenue vs. $35.85B est.) and enthusiasm over its Nasdaq ADR plan, SK Hynix shares surged +13.06% on June 25 to 2.9 million won as KOSPI jumped +5.42%. At 2.9M won/share and 1,542.7 KRW/USD, the authorized 17.79 million new shares imply ~51.59 trillion won (~$33.4B), well above the board's 45.45 trillion won (~$29.5B) fundraising cap—giving SK Hynix a substantially wider cushion to clear Alibaba's $25B foreign U.S. IPO record even after a typical 10-15% ADR pricing discount. With bookbuilding scheduled for July 7 and pricing/debut on July 10 (and outlets like The Straits Times directly benchmarking the deal against Alibaba's 2014 record), SK Hynix moves up to 71%, while Alibaba retains 28% for SEC Form F-1 schedule slip past July 10, extreme KOSPI volatility, or definitional reporting treating an ADR cross-listing separately from a traditional IPO.

questions.title: Which country will agree to a joint project with Iran to clear sea mines from the Strait of Hormuz by August 26, 2026?
questions.background: Sea mines have been reported near the Strait of Hormuz, a major route for international oil and gas shipments.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the country that agrees with Iran to a joint mine-clearance project in the Strait of Hormuz, as announced in a statement from the two governments by August 26, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-08-26 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: June 25 local reporting (Al Jazeera, Straits Times, NDTV, Baird Maritime) brings two meaningful updates: (1) IRGC-Oman friction flared as the IRGC publicly rejected Oman's IMO-backed southern shipping corridor (monitored by the US Navy) as unauthorized and 'unacceptable,' Oman's FM Badr Albusaidi pushed back against Iranian transit fees, and a cargo vessel was attacked near Oman, pausing the UN evacuation plan—trimming Oman from 0.36 to 0.31, though Oman remains the #1 favorite given the June 23 Muscat bilateral working-group statement; (2) Al Jazeera explicitly grouped Japan with the UK/France-led Western demining effort ('France and the United Kingdom are leading the demining effort, backed by allies including Germany, Italy, Japan and Canada') on the same day Iran's Foreign Ministry furiously condemned NATO/European complicity and pre-positioned European demining assets—lowering Japan from 0.12 to 0.08. Shifted mass goes to non-Western partners acceptable to Tehran: China (0.21, top Iranian oil buyer with strong MCM capability), Russia (0.12), and Pakistan (0.11, Islamabad MoU broker with minehunters), leaving 17% tail mass.

local_articles.title: Ships crossing Strait of Hormuz use Oman passage despite Iran warnings
local_articles.snippet: LONDON – Traffic levels in the Strait of Hormuz fell back from a June 24 high, but vessels continued to use a non-Iranian-approved passage despite a ship being struck by a projectile, tracking platforms showed on June 26. At least 42 commodity vessels – including tankers carrying oil, gas, and dry bulk such as fertilisers – crossed on June 25, Kpler’s tracking platform showed, down from a high of 57 on June 24. Ten of those vessels entered the Gulf, while 32 exited. Half of the 42 vessels used a southern passageway hugging the coast of Oman. Another 29 commodity vessels had already crossed the strait by afternoon of June 26, 10 coming into the Gulf and 19 leaving, according to Kpler. local_articles.title: Why has the UN paused plans to evacuate sailors from the Strait of Hormuz?
local_articles.snippet: The United Nations’ International Maritime Organization (IMO) has suspended plans to evacuate more than 11,000 sailors stranded in the Strait of Hormuz after a cargo ship transiting the waterway was struck by a projectile. IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez said several crews had already been evacuated, but the agency had decided to pause the operation until there were “necessary safety guarantees” for those involved.
